info.title: Ybug API
info.description: Ybug API specification for user, team, project and feedback management endpoints. > **⚠️ Availability:** The API is currently limited to Company and Enterprise plan customers. ### Base url ``` https://api.ybug.io ``` ### Authentication All requests must be authenticated using a **Bearer Token** passed in the `Authorization` header. ``` Authorization: Bearer ``` ### Getting Your API Token To generate your personal API token, log in to your Ybug Dashboard and navigate to the Profile settings section: Ybug Dashboard. Click the "Generate token" button to create and view your token. ### Error Handling We utilize **Standardized HTTP Status Codes** and return **structured JSON error bodies** to ensure predictable and full error handling across all endpoints. | Status | Meaning | Typical Cause | | ------ | ------- | ------------- | | 400 Bad Request | The request payload or query parameters are invalid. | Validation errors, missing required fields, malformed JSON. | | 401 Unauthorized | The request lacks valid authentication credentials. | Missing or expired bearer token. | | 403 Forbidden | The authenticated token cannot access the resource. | Insufficient permissions, plan limitations. | | 404 Not Found | The requested resource does not exist. | Incorrect IDs or deleted resources. | | 429 Too Many Requests | The client exceeded the rate limit. | More than 100 requests per minute. | | 500 Internal Server Error | An unexpected error occurred on the server. | Transient server issues; retry with backoff. | ### Rate Limits The current global rate limit is **100 requests per minute (RPM)** per authenticated client. Exceeding this limit will result in an **HTTP 429 Too Many Requests** response.

get.description: Returns the profile information for the user associated with the API token, including basic identity fields and timestamps.

200.description: Successful retrieval of the authorized user profile.

get.description: Lists every team accessible to the current API token, reflecting the user’s membership and plan entitlements.

200.description: Successful retrieval of the list of teams.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: When true, returns archived projects instead of active ones.

get.description: Retrieves a paginated collection of projects within the specified team that the token may access. Supports toggling archived projects with the `archived` query parameter.

200.description: Successful retrieval of the projects list for the team.

post.description: Creates a new project within the specified team. Provide the desired name in the request body; the response returns the newly created project resource.

name.description: The desired name for the new project.

get.description: Retrieves a paginated list of projects available to the API token across all teams. Use the `archived` query parameter to switch between active and archived projects.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: When true, returns archived projects instead of active ones.

200.description: Successful retrieval of the list of projects.

get.description: Fetches full details for the specified project, including identifiers, status, and timestamps.

200.description: Successful retrieval of project details.

patch.description: Updates editable fields on the project, such as the name or archived status. Send only the attributes that should change.

name.description: The new name for the project.

status.description: The project's current status (e.g., used for archiving).

200.description: Project successfully updated.

delete.description: Permanently removes the specified project. Only projects the token can manage may be deleted.

get.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of feedback items captured on the project. Results default to ascending creation order and can be sorted via the `order_by` parameter.
Optional `assignee[]` filters restrict results to the OR of selected assignees or unassigned (pass a special value `none`).
Optional `tag[]` filters restrict results to feedback that has at least one of the given tags (OR). Each value is a tag name or tag UUID for the project's team.
Optional `status[]` filters restrict results to feedback in any of the given statuses (OR). Each value is a `status_id` for the project's team; the comma-separated `status=1,2` form works too.

200.description: Successful retrieval of feedback for the project.

get.description: Returns the list of project members. These users can be used for feedback assignment.

200.description: Successful retrieval of project members.

get.description: Returns all webhook subscriptions configured for the project, allowing clients to inspect existing destinations and statuses.

200.description: Successful retrieval of webhooks for the project.

post.description: Registers a new webhook endpoint for the project. Provide the desired event and HTTPS target URL; optionally include a secret for request signing.

event.description: Event that triggers the webhook. Currently, only feedback.created is supported per project.

target_url.description: HTTPS endpoint that receives the webhook payload.

secret.description: Optional shared secret used to sign webhook payloads.

409.description: Conflict. A webhook for the specified event already exists for this project.

get.description: Retrieves configuration details for a specific webhook on the project, including the target URL and activation state.

200.description: Successful retrieval of the webhook details.

delete.description: Removes the specified webhook subscription from the project. After deletion, no further events are sent to the target URL.

post.description: Queues a synthetic event for the webhook to validate connectivity and payload handling by the target URL.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the feedback item.

get.description: Retrieves the full feedback record, including metadata, reporter context, and any associated assets.

200.description: Successful retrieval of the feedback item.

patch.description: Updates one or more mutable fields on the feedback record, such as status, priority, assignee, or descriptive text. Only provided attributes are modified.

schema.description: One or more updatable fields of a feedback item.

status_id.description:
New status identifier. Must be one of the team's statuses, as listed by
`GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/statuses`; anything else is rejected with a **400**
listing the ids the project accepts. Ids 1-5 are the built-in statuses (Open,
In progress, Resolved, Closed, Backlog), custom statuses start at 100.

Feedback always has a status; it cannot be cleared with `null`.

assignee_id.description:
Assign feedback to a project member by their user UUID.

Set to `null` to unassign.

title.description: New feedback title (HTML tags will be stripped).

description.description: New feedback description (HTML tags will be stripped).
description.example: When I click submit, nothing happens.

200.description: Feedback successfully updated.

delete.description: Permanently removes the feedback record. Linked assets and references are also cleared.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the feedback item.

post.description: Adds the provided tags to the feedback item without removing existing ones. Tag names that do not yet exist are auto-created at the team level. Tags already present are ignored.

tags.description: Array of tag names to add. Duplicates are ignored.

200.description: Tags successfully added.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the feedback item.

parameters.name: tagNameOrId
parameters.description: Tag name or tag UUID to remove from the feedback item.

delete.description: Removes the specified tag from the feedback item. If the tag is not currently assigned, the operation is a no-op.

200.description: Tag successfully removed (or was not present). Returns the list of remaining tags.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the feedback item.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of non-deleted comments on the specified feedback item. Supports ordering by `created_at`.

200.description: Successful retrieval of comments.

post.description:
Creates a new comment on the feedback item. The authenticated user is set as the author.
Comments are internal (private team notes) by default. Set `internal` to `false` to create a public reply to notify the reporter.

body.description: The comment body (max 500 characters, HTML stripped).
body.example: Can you try clearing your cache?

internal.description: When true, the comment is a private team comment. When false, it is a public reply visible to the reporter. Defaults to true.

patch.description: Updates the text of an internal (private) comment. Public replies cannot be edited — returns 400 if attempted.

body.description: The updated comment body (max 500 characters, HTML stripped).
body.example: Updated: can you try a hard refresh?

200.description: Comment successfully updated.

get.description: Returns all tags in the team.

200.description: Successful retrieval of tags.

post.description: Creates a new tag in the team. The tag name must be unique within the team.

name.description: The tag name (max 30 characters, HTML stripped).

get.description: Retrieves details for a specific tag.

200.description: Successful retrieval of the tag.

patch.description: Renames an existing tag. The new name must be unique within the owning team.

name.description: The new tag name (max 30 characters, HTML stripped).

200.description: Tag successfully updated.

delete.description: Permanently removes the tag. Any feedback associations are also removed.

get.description:
Returns the team's whole feedback status workflow, ordered by `position`. Every one of these is
valid in every project of the team.
Status ids are per team, so a status is only ever meaningful together with the team it came from.

200.description: Successful retrieval of the team's statuses.

get.description:
Returns the statuses valid for feedback in this project, ordered by `position`, and therefore the
exact set of ids `status_id` accepts when updating feedback. Every team status is valid in every
one of its projects, so this is the same list as `GET /v1/teams/{teamId}/statuses`, reached through
project access instead of team access. A project may hide a status from its own board and quick
filters; that is a display preference and such statuses are still listed, assignable and filterable.

200.description: Successful retrieval of the project's statuses.

BearerAuth.description: API token provided in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.

BadRequestError.description: Bad Request. The request was invalid (e.g., missing required fields in payload).

UnauthorizedError.description: Unauthorized. Missing or invalid API token.

ForbiddenError.description: Forbidden. The user does not have permission to access the resource, or the operation is restricted by the account plan.

NotFoundError.description: Not Found. The requested resource (team or project ID) could not be found.

ConflictError.description: Conflict. A resource with the same unique identifier already exists.

TooManyRequestsError.description: Too Many Requests. The rate limit for the client has been exceeded.

InternalServerError.description: Internal Server Error. An unexpected error occurred on the server.

Page.name: page
Page.description: The page number to retrieve. Starts at 1.

PageSize.name: page_size
PageSize.description: Number of items per page (defaults to 25, maximum 100).

OrderBy.name: order_by
OrderBy.description: Order results by given field with asc|desc direction. Format is "field:asc" or "field:desc".

AssigneeFilter.name: assignee
AssigneeFilter.description:
Repeatable filter (e.g. `assignee[]=uuid&assignee[]=none`). Each value is combined with **OR**.
Pass a user UUID (same as `assignee.id` on a feedback item) or the keyword `none` for unassigned feedback.
Returns **400** if any value is neither `none` nor a valid UUID.

TagFilter.name: tag

StatusFilter.name: status
StatusFilter.description:
Repeatable filter (e.g. `status[]=1&status[]=2`); the comma-separated `status=1,2` form
works too. Each value is combined with **OR**. Values are `status_id`s from
`GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/statuses`; ids the team does not have are ignored,
and if none of them resolve, the list is empty.

errors.description: A list of human-readable error messages.

total_count.description: The total number of items available across all pages.

page.description: The current page number being returned (starts at 1).

page_size.description: Number of items per page (25 by default, max 100).

last_page.description: True if this is the final page of results.

user_data.description: Arbitrary user-provided data associated with the feedback.

plan.description: Example custom key. Actual keys are user-defined.

user_id.description: Example custom key. Actual keys are user-defined.

description.example: When I click submit, nothing happens.

status_id.description:
The status of the feedback, as a `status_id` of the project's team. See the `status_id`
request field on "Update feedback" for how the id ranges work.

comment_count.description: Number of comments on this feedback item.

tags.description: Tags assigned to this feedback item.

custom_fields.description: Custom fields configured for the feedback item project.

status_id.description:
The status identifier, unique **within its team**. The built-in statuses hold the same
ids in every team (1 Open, 2 In progress, 3 Resolved, 4 Closed, and 5 Backlog for teams
that have it) and can only be renamed, recoloured and repositioned. Custom statuses are
numbered per team from 100 up, so id 100 means a different status in another team.

Within a team an id is stable and never reused, even after the status is deleted.

category.description:
The workflow meaning of the status. Branch on this rather than on the name, which
teams are free to change, or on `status_id`, which is stable but says nothing about
meaning: a team may have several statuses of one category, or none of another.

color.description:
The colour the status is drawn in, as a palette token rather than a hex value. Teams
pick from this fixed set, so the value is always one of the ones below. Always present:
a status with no colour of its own takes the colour of its `category` (`open` blue,
`in_progress` orange, `resolved` green, `closed` slate, `backlog` gray).

A token is stable; the hex behind it is not, and may be retuned in a redesign. Map it to
your own palette rather than storing our pixels. The hex Ybug currently draws each token
in, as `text` on `background`:

| Token | Text | Background |
| ----- | ---- | ---------- |
| `blue` | `#0284FF` | `#E0F2FE` |
| `indigo` | `#4444DD` | `#EDEDFB` |
| `purple` | `#9333EA` | `#F3E8FF` |
| `pink` | `#DB2777` | `#FCE7F3` |
| `red` | `#E5231B` | `#FFE3E0` |
| `orange` | `#FF8800` | `#FFF1DB` |
| `yellow` | `#CA8A04` | `#FEF9C3` |
| `green` | `#16C264` | `#DCFCE7` |
| `teal` | `#0D9488` | `#CCFBF1` |
| `slate` | `#5B6678` | `#EEF1F6` |
| `gray` | `#98A2B3` | `#F2F4F7` |

position.description: Sort order within the team, ascending. Ordering is free-form and does not follow `category`.

built_in.description:
Whether this is a built-in status, i.e. one Ybug ships rather than one the team added.
Built-ins can be renamed and recoloured but never deleted, and always have a `status_id`
below 100; custom statuses start at 100.

Ids 1-5 are the built-in slots (Open, In progress, Resolved, Closed, Backlog) and 6-99
are reserved for future built-ins. Do not assume a team has all of them: teams created
before Backlog existed start with 1-4 only. List the statuses instead.

value.description: Custom field value. Null when no value was submitted for this feedback item.

body.example: Can you try clearing your cache?

internal.description: True if this is a private team comment (note), false if it is a public reply.

id.description: Author user UUID. Null for inbound email replies.
